qs.q: The chemical pathology syllabus requires students to understand enzyme kinetics in disease states. Why is this topic emphasized in Year Three pathology training?
o: Guide interpretation of organ‑damage diagnostic assays
qs.e: Enzyme kinetics form the theoretical basis for interpreting specific organ damage diagnostic assays.
qs.s: Weekly Year 3: Reference Exam - November 6, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: An investigator measures enzyme kinetics and finds that adding compound X increases the apparent Km without changing the Vmax. How does compound X interact with the enzyme?
o: It binds covalently to catalytic residues blocking substrate entry permanently.
It binds an allosteric site altering the three-dimensional protein conformation.
It binds reversibly to the active site competing directly with the substrate.
It destroys the tertiary structure of the protein causing irreversible denaturation.
It reacts with the reaction product shifting equilibrium toward reactants.
qs.e: Competitive inhibitors raise apparent Km by competing for the active site, which can be overcome by high substrate concentrations.
qs.s: Weekly Year 1: Biochemistry Exam - October 30, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)
